additional_info.subject: RE: AW: AW: ID0474105-DC/Si-D/AT- [Y2/T3314161484002] Charging Issue CRM:03289000343
additional_info.body:
Dear Laurenz,
Thank you for the reply.
Insulation can occur for several reason: mechanical damage/ physical damage
(Abrasion/Friction, over used, crushing): Please check in cable head, if found any observable damage.
Water ingression, chemical exposure like oil or other substances in the cable head, Electrical damage ( like voltage issue).
But as the problem re-occurring, in my opinion its maybe mechanical/ physical damage of the cable. Please do the following:
1. Visual inspect: Looks for cracks, cuts abrasion or swelling of the cable.
2. Please perform a insulation Resistance tests: Using a megger to measure the insulation resistance can be identify degradation.
If its found sign of wire. We may need to replace the cable.

additional_info.subject: Summary of findings
additional_info.body:
The ticket reports a Jaguar I‑Pace failing to charge on a Sicharge D, but it does not include vehicle details in the contact form. The ticket mentions a failure during
cable check
at
11:44
, but the logged sessions did
not
fail during the cable check phase. Instead, the failure occurred during the
charging phase
.
At
2026‑01‑21 11:33:26
, during phase
P06_CHARGE
, the charger detected an
“Iso fault by IMD output relay.”
Two seconds later, the IMD reported:
“PLC‑Error‑Flag ‘IMD_BC1’ initial value true – Insulation resistance below alarm level (1 kΩ).”
This occurred during the transition
PilotState B2 → E
, indicating that charging was interrupted due to insulation resistance dropping below the allowed threshold. As PilotState B2 was logged during the fault, this means that the 1 kΩ reading reflects the reading of whatever is after the IMD device, i.e. the EV.
Logs are attached.
Conclusion:
The charging interruption was caused by an
isolation fault detected by the IMD
, not a cable check failure.
Next Steps:
If the region would like the TS team to perform further investigation, this must be requested via a
new ticket
, as the current process doesn't allow the reopening of a resolved ticket. The Product Champion and the Austrian team will align on how to proceed.
